newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank urges Dutch to act on bonds before euro.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank urges Dutch to act on bonds before euro.

text.p: Dutch cooperative Rabobank has warned that Amsterdam's position as a financial centre could be in jeopardy if business in state bonds leaked to other European markets after Economic and Monetary Union and the introduction of the single currency -- the euro.

"The Dutch government should issue some big state bonds in euro's in 1999 and pay off the old guilder bonds," Rabobank chairman Herman Wijffels told a conference, adding that business in Dutch state bonds could be lost to other financial centres if the Dutch government failed to address this problem.
The Dutch state could also issue new longer-dated ECU bonds next year and change them into euro-bonds once the euro became legal tender. "We should set a benchmark," Wijffels said.
He added that Dutch banks and financial institutes would continue talks on Wednesday to set a timetable for their clients, both private and corporate, for when they could begin using the euro.

"It's very likely that big firms, along with the share market, will start using the euro as official currency from January 1999," he said, adding that private clients and the retail sector would probably have to wait until 2002.

"They (retailers) do not want to start on January 1, 2002, as planned, but later, as they foresee problems during the New Year sales period," he said, adding that February 4, 2002 would be a more likely start-date.
